section: Non-residents: employment income
label: Who is a non-resident taxpayer (buitenlands belastingplichtige)
value: Someone who does not live in the Netherlands but has Dutch income
note: Tax treaties decide which country may tax pay for work done in the Netherlands; the period in which the 183 days are counted differs per treaty. Someone who lives abroad but is insured in the Netherlands also pays national insurance premiums on box 1 income.
source_title: Belastingdienst: Fiscale informatie 2026, chapter 30 U woont buiten Nederland; Wet inkomstenbelasting 2001, articles 2.1 and 7.2 (wetten.overheid.nl, version of 1 January 2026)

section: Non-residents: employment income
label: Residence test
value: Judged on the facts and circumstances: a lasting personal tie with the Netherlands, where the person's social and economic life is centred (for someone without a family, also the intention to settle); the law sets no day count
note: Tax treaties decide which country may tax pay for work done in the Netherlands; the period in which the 183 days are counted differs per treaty. Someone who lives abroad but is insured in the Netherlands also pays national insurance premiums on box 1 income.
source_title: Algemene wet inzake rijksbelastingen, article 4 (wetten.overheid.nl, version of 1 January 2026); Belastingdienst: Handboek Loonheffingen 2026, version October 2026, paragraph 2.3.3 (printed page 41)

section: Non-residents: employment income
label: What a non-resident pays income tax on
value: Box 1 income tax at the normal rates on pay for work done in the Netherlands, and on other Dutch income such as profit from a Dutch permanent establishment
note: Tax treaties decide which country may tax pay for work done in the Netherlands; the period in which the 183 days are counted differs per treaty. Someone who lives abroad but is insured in the Netherlands also pays national insurance premiums on box 1 income.
source_title: Belastingdienst: Fiscale informatie 2026, chapter 30 U woont buiten Nederland; Wet inkomstenbelasting 2001, articles 2.1 and 7.2 (wetten.overheid.nl, version of 1 January 2026)

section: Contractors: employment test, Wet DBA and model agreements
label: Official test: employee or self-employed
value: Employment has three marks: the possibility of employer authority (gezag), the obligation to do the work personally, and pay for the work; all facts and circumstances are weighed (nature and length of the work, how work and hours are set, integration in the client's organisation, commercial risk, behaving as an entrepreneur)
note: A client who wrongly treats an employee as self-employed must correct the payroll tax returns and pay the wage taxes, with interest on a back assessment.
source_title: Belastingdienst: Wanneer is er sprake van loondienst? (arbeidsrelaties)

section: Contractors: employment test, Wet DBA and model agreements
label: Fictitious employment (fictieve dienstbetrekking)
value: Some contractors count as employees by law, so the client withholds wage taxes: for example people who usually work 2 or more days a week and earn at least 2/5 of the minimum wage (gelijkgestelden), homeworkers, artists and professional athletes, and workers placed through an intermediary; for gelijkgestelden, homeworkers and artists both parties can opt out in writing before the first payment
note: A client who wrongly treats an employee as self-employed must correct the payroll tax returns and pay the wage taxes, with interest on a back assessment.

label: Wet DBA enforcement
value: Normal rules since 1 January 2025 (end of the enforcement moratorium): correction orders and back assessments directly; penalties for gross negligence or intent from 1 January 2026; no default penalties in 2026; back assessments not before 1 January 2025 unless in bad faith (then up to 5 years)
note: A client who wrongly treats an employee as self-employed must correct the payroll tax returns and pay the wage taxes, with interest on a back assessment.

section: Property tax: onroerendezaakbelastingen (OZB)
label: What it is
value: A municipal tax on real estate: owners of homes and of non-residential property pay an owners' tax; users of non-residential property pay a users' tax
note: Gemeentewet, articles 220 to 220h. The WOZ value also sets other charges, such as the water authority levy on buildings.
source_title: Gemeentewet, articles 220 to 220h (wetten.overheid.nl, version of 1 January 2026)

section: Property tax: onroerendezaakbelastingen (OZB)
label: Base
value: The WOZ value set for the year under the Valuation of Immovable Property Act (Wet waardering onroerende zaken)
note: Gemeentewet, articles 220 to 220h. The WOZ value also sets other charges, such as the water authority levy on buildings.
source_title: Gemeentewet, articles 220 to 220h (wetten.overheid.nl, version of 1 January 2026)

section: Property tax: onroerendezaakbelastingen (OZB)
label: Rates
value: A percentage of the WOZ value, set each year by each municipality in its tax ordinance, separately for owners of homes, owners of non-residential property and users of non-residential property; the law sets no national rate or cap
note: Gemeentewet, articles 220 to 220h. The WOZ value also sets other charges, such as the water authority levy on buildings.
source_title: Gemeentewet, articles 220 to 220h (wetten.overheid.nl, version of 1 January 2026)

section: Property tax: onroerendezaakbelastingen (OZB)
label: Who pays
value: Whoever owns or uses the property on 1 January pays for the whole year; for a home only the owner pays
note: Gemeentewet, articles 220 to 220h. The WOZ value also sets other charges, such as the water authority levy on buildings.
source_title: Ondernemersplein (RVO): Onroerendezaakbelasting (OZB) voor bedrijfspand betalen (checked 30 September 2026), with links to each municipality's OZB rates

label: Simplified regimes: small business scheme (kleineondernemersregeling, KOR) [national]
value: VAT exemption for turnover up to €20,000 a calendar year; EU-KOR up to €100,000 of EU turnover; no presumptive income tax. Paid by no one: it is an exemption that small businesses can opt into. Wet op de omzetbelasting 1968.

value: box 1 income tax at the normal rates on pay for work in the Netherlands, withheld by the employer; tax part of the tax credits only for qualifying non-residents (90% test) and, for the labour tax credit, residents of the EU, EEA, Switzerland and the BES islands. Paid by non-resident employees (withheld by the employer). Wet inkomstenbelasting 2001, articles 2.1 and 7.2; Algemene wet inzake rijksbelastingen, article 4 (residence).
